The primitive rational normal for the affine span of lattice points in an arbitrary real hyperplane has at least one odd coefficient. The plane x_1=1 has vertices on both sides, and the supporting plane x_1=0 contains exactly seven.

For all ε in the stated range, each fiber of the actual lifted hull at an integer vertex is exactly its prescribed full-dimensional simplex. The barycentric upper bounds at other bases are at most one for identical fibers and at most (B/A)^(1/d)≤(8/7)^(1/d) for positive ε, so the specified exposing tilt strictly excludes all other fibers.

The canonical cap family gives the pointwise global upper bound, and an exposed largest-fiber centroid gives the matching lower bound. Total mass is 16v. The internal plane has mass 8A/16, all other planes have at most 7B/16, and the inequalities agree at ε=1/30.
